analysis: The only change is scripts/test-provider-release-resume.py line 296: the workflow-guard test now also asserts that the `qualify-sdk-shard` job in release-provider.yml carries `if: needs.resolve-env.outputs.resume != 'true'`, alongside `build-provider` and `qualify-sdk`. This is a test-only tightening that checks a release-recovery control. It adds no runtime code, attack surface or trust change. It touches the release and recovery pipeline (A-011 and A-017 territory, build provenance and qualification), not provider runtime, TB-002 or TB-011 behavior. The test uses str.split on the workflow text. If `qualify-sdk-shard` were missing or renamed in the workflow, the test would fail with an IndexError. That is a fail-closed outcome for a test and not a security issue. I did not see the workflow file, so I cannot confirm that `qualify-sdk-shard` exists and is correctly guarded there. The sign-gate truth-table test at lines 280-295 is unchanged and still enforces that signing runs only when resume is true and build and qualify are skipped, or resume is false and both succeed. One integration question remains: whether release-provider.yml, which is outside the supplied evidence, defines the shard job so that the sign job's `needs` and result checks cover a skipped or failed shard on the non-resume path. This is unverified and not a finding.
